job-title: Front brake pads and rotors
job-setting: Small independent shop, customer's sedan on the floor, and the only lift is taken.

line 1: Jess
Car's on the ground, cracking the lug nuts loose on both front wheels before I lift it.

line 2: Jess
Rear wheels are chocked. Floor jack under the front center jacking point, lifting till both front tires are off the ground.

line 3: Jess
Lift's taken, so I'll just leave it sitting up on the floor jack. I'm only gonna be in the wheel wells for a few minutes.

explain-panel: What's wrong, and why?
🎤 Talk
Submit
explain-input: Never work under a car held up only by the jack, put it on jack stands so it cannot fall and crush you
feedback-text: Good catch. A jack is for lifting, not holding. A hydraulic jack can bleed down or roll, and Jess's hands and arms are in the wheel well the whole job.

line 4: Jess
Wheels off. Pulling the caliper bolts and the bracket bolts on the driver side.

explain-panel: What's wrong, and why?
🎤 Talk
Submit
feedback-text: That step was actually fine. Stopping the job costs time, so save the STOP for real hazards.

line 5: Jess
Letting the caliper hang off the brake hose while I swap the rotor.

line 6: Jess
Wire brushed the rust off the hub, new rotor's on and wiped down with brake cleaner. Fluid level's checked, now pushing the piston back with the old pad and a C clamp.

line 7: Jess
Pads in with new clips, slide pins greased, caliper's back on. Running the bracket bolts in with the impact, a couple good hits and they're tight.

line 8: Jess
Same on the other side. Wheels on, lugs run down snug, car's back on the ground, then torquing the lugs in a star pattern.

line 9: Jess
Pumping the pedal till it's firm, checking the fluid level again, and taking it around the block to bed in the pads before I hand the keys back.
result-summary: Caught 1 of 3 mistakes · 1 false alarm

missed-list: MINOR · MISSED · -25 PTS

Let the caliper hang by its brake hose. The hose tore on the inside and started trapping pressure. The customer came back a month later with that brake dragging and the car pulling to one side.

Should have: Hang the caliper from the spring or strut with a hook, a bungee, or a piece of wire so there's no strain on the hose.

MAJOR · MISSED · -75 PTS

Ran the bracket bolts in with an impact, no torque. One bracket bolt backed out over the next few weeks. The customer came back with a grinding clunk when braking, and the shop paid for a new rotor, a bracket, and a chewed up wheel.

Should have: Start the bolts by hand, then tighten them with a torque wrench to the factory spec, with thread locker if the manual calls for it.
